Il y a un payable en attente de 800,00 $ (payable A ) et deux créances existantes dont les soldes respectifs s’élèvent à 2 000,00 $ (créance C ) et 1 000,00 $ (créance D ). Chaque mois, la retenue de la pension de RET et de la pension de SURV est de 25 %. Après une réévaluation du compte, un payable supplémentaire de 300,00 $ (payable B ) est dû au client. L’utilisateur applique le montant de recouvrement de créance de remplacement de 150,00 $ entre 800,00 $ (payable A ) et 2 000,00 $ (créance C ). Le payable A est de 800,00 $ Le payable B est de 300,00 $ La créance C est de 2 000,00 $ avec un taux de recouvrement récurrent de 25 % La créance D est de 1 000,00 $ avec un taux de recouvrement récurrent de 25 % Le payable A (800,00 $) plus le payable B (300,00 $) est un payable brut global de 1 100,00 $. Par conséquent : Le payable A (800,00 $) servira à appliquer le recouvrement unique de 150,00 $ à la créance C (2 000,00 $) = 150,00 $ Le payable A (800,00 $) × le taux de recouvrement de 25 % pour la créance D (1 000,00 $) = 200,00 $ Le payable B (300,00 $) × le taux de recouvrement de 25 % pour la créance C (2 000,00 $) = 75,00 $ Le payable B (300,00 $) × le taux de recouvrement de 25 % pour la créance D = 75,00 $ 150,00 $ + 75,00 $ = 225,00 $, qui représente la déduction globale pour la créance C 75 $ + 200 $ = 275 $, qui représente la déduction globale pour la créance D Le payable brut de 1 100,00 $ − 225,00 $ − 275,00 $ = Montant net de 600,00 $ (paiement hebdomadaire)

item1_text: Callout Example 1 The client was incarcerated on February 15, 2018, and was released from incarceration on April 11, 2023. The incarceration dates were confirmed with the Correctional Service of Canada data transfer. The client turned 65 on March 6, 2021. In April 2023, upon their release from incarceration, they applied for their OAS pension and indicated that they have lived in Canada since birth. In normal circumstances, the client would be entitled to 24 months of actuarial adjustment for the period of April 2021 (the earliest date of eligibility) and their effective date of April 2023 (the month of their release). However, since this client has been incarcerated since 2018 (i.e. before their 65th birthday), they are not entitled to any deferral for the period of April 2021 to April 2023.
item2_text: Callout Example 2 The client was incarcerated on November 12, 2020, and was released from incarceration on July 5, 2024. The incarceration dates were confirmed with the Correctional Service of Canada data transfer. The client turned 65 on November 16, 2022. On August 12, 2024, after being released from incarceration, the client applied for their OAS pension and the GIS . The client is not entitled to the GIS as their income is in excess. They have provided the following residence history: Birth to May 31, 1993: Italy June 1, 1993 to present: Canada In normal circumstances, the client would receive a choice between: 31/40ths effective July 2024; or 29/40ths with 19 months of actuarial adjustment effective July 2024. Since this client was incarcerated before their 65th birthday, the residence can accumulate up until the month the pension is approved. However, the client is not entitled to accrue an actuarial adjustment for the months they were incarcerated. Therefore, in this situation, no pension choices would be offered to the client. Their pension would be approved effective July 2024 at a rate of 31/40ths.

Passage 1 states the school year ends in April 2025 and the vacation period runs from May 2025 to mid-September 2025, while Passage 2 states the school year ends in June 2025 and the vacation period starts in July 2025. Additionally, Passage 1 claims the child is deemed to be in full-time attendance until September 2025, whereas Passage 2 indicates that the student cannot be considered in full-time attendance for the 2025-2026 school year despite being deemed as attending full-time during the illness period. These discrepancies create mutually incompatible claims regarding the student's attendance and benefits.
item1_text: Callout Example A student submits a completed ISP-1402 form and it is approved. The school year starts September 2024 and ends April 2025. The vacation period runs from May 2025 until the middle of September 2025, when school resumes again. The student advises the Department that they stopped attending school due to illness as of December 2024. To support their claim they submit an ISP-1403 form to confirm they cannot resume full-time attendance at school during that academic year. You must not suspend the child's benefit in this situation as the child is deemed to be in full-time attendance until the end of the school vacation period (i.e. until September 2025).
item2_text: Callout Example A student submits an ISP-1402 form and it is approved. The school year starts in September 2024 and ends in June 2025. The vacation period starts in July 2025 and ends in September 2025. In December 2024, the student stops attending school due to an illness. To support their claim, they submit an ISP-1403 form that covers the 2024-2025 academic year and vacation period. Their child's benefit payments will continue for the remainder of the 2024-2025 academic year, including the summer vacation period. The student does not resume school attendance during the 2025-2026 or 2026-2027 academic years but is able to return to school or university on a full-time basis in the 2027-2028 school year. Due to this, the student cannot be considered to have been in full-time attendance for the 2025-2026 school year, even though they were deemed as attending full-time during their illness period from December 2024 to September 2025. To be entitled, the student must have submitted an ISP-1403 form and resumed attendance immediately after the period of illness. If the student is absent for the entire year, they will only be entitled to benefits if they resume attendance in the following academic year and submit a second ISP-1403 form to support the entire period of the absence (including the vacation period).
